summary: IsOwnTermMatrixTest.java reviewed by tracing all 4 test methods x 2 parameterized cases against LeaseManager's acquireLocked/renewLocked/releaseLocked/refreshed/isOwnTerm, and by empirically mutating production code in a scratch copy (restored, diff-clean afterward). Confirmed `git diff` on production shows no residual change and only the intended test file is staged. Ran the suite for real: 8/8 pass against the true isOwnTerm. Applying the podId-dropped mutation (`return current.epoch() == mine.epoch();`) empirically fails exactly the 4 POD_ID cases (one per method) and leaves all 4 EPOCH cases green -- matches the author's claim exactly. Applying the epoch-boundary widening the reviewer was asked to stress (`current.epoch() >= mine.epoch()`) empirically fails exactly the 4 EPOCH cases and leaves all 4 POD_ID cases green -- so the 'fenced process treated as owning a higher epoch too' mutation the task asked about is caught, not a surviving gap. Traced (and for the release path, confirmed by mental execution against Lease.renewedUntil/Lease.equals) that releaseRecoveryRefusesASingleMismatchedConjunct's discriminator is not vacuous: under an isOwnTerm-always-true mutant, release's refreshed() adopts the other holder's/successor's live lease as belief and then writes an expired copy of it over the real live lease, so the store's lease measurably changes and the byte-identity assertion against `liveHolder` (captured before release()) fails -- for both the EPOCH cell (adopts and expires the genuine successor's epoch-2 lease) and the POD_ID cell (adopts and expires the out-of-protocol other-holder's lease). Checked the two-stage clock advances in the renew/release fixtures (advance past RENEW, then past TTL): the EPOCH cell's 'genuine takeover' setup lands the new manager's tryAcquire exactly on Lease.isExpiredAt's documented inclusive `>=` boundary (nowMillis == expiresAtMillis), which is deterministic under the fake TestClock (no wall-clock, no sleep) rather than a source of flakiness; it does make that setup step incidentally coupled to isExpiredAt's own boundary correctness, but a mutation there would fail the fixture's own setup assertion (`...tryAcquire()).isPresent()`) rather than silently passing, so it is not a hidden false-negative for isOwnTerm. Checked whether this file alone would catch a `return false;` (or `!(...)`) mutation of isOwnTerm: it would not, because every one of the 8 fixtures is deliberately constructed so the correct answer is already false (this is a stated, deliberate 'negative-control' matrix, per its own class javadoc) -- but this is not a project-level gap: LeaseManagerAcquireAmbiguityTest#anAcquisitionThatLandedButLostItsResponseIsFoundOnTheNextTry and LeaseManagerAmbiguityTest#aReleaseWhoseSuccessfulRefreshIsFollowedByAFailedWriteKeepsTheRefreshedBelief already exercise the true/positive branch of isOwnTerm at the acquire-recovery and release sites respectively (asserting held()/tryAcquire() isPresent() after a genuine same-term recovery), so a constant-false mutant is killed by the pre-existing suite; recorded as a scope note only. Checked .harness/tdd/red.json: all 4 method-level ids (theUnexpiredBranchRefusesASingleMismatchedConjunct, acquireRecoveryRefusesASingleMismatchedConjunct, renewRecoveryRefusesASingleMismatchedConjunct, releaseRecoveryRefusesASingleMismatchedConjunct) are present with sha256-keyed records; check-tdd.sh is already listed as passed in the review packet, which is the gate that verifies those records bind to the current staged content -- did not re-implement that binding-key computation by hand, per the review packet's instruction not to re-check gates that already passed. No existing assertion was weakened (this is a new file only; git status shows no other tracked file staged). No Thread.sleep, no system temp, no real clock/socket -- MemoryBinStore and a hand-rolled deterministic TestClock, consistent with testing.md and non-negotiable 7. Enumeration matches the class's own claim: 2 lexical call sites x 4 reachable paths (tryAcquire's unexpired branch; refreshed() via acquire-recovery, renewLocked, releaseLocked), all 4 present as methods, no path missing.
